prose: The PyTorch team introduces TorchNeuron, a native PyTorch backend for AWS Trainium that runs standard model code on Amazon's AI chips without Neuron-specific adaptation, expanding hardware choice while keeping the familiar eager execution and distributed APIs. Cartesia reports its Sonic and Ink voice models ran through the native path with minimal changes, leaving hand-written NKI kernels only for the hot layers that drive end-to-end latency. Deepgram, after a multi-month port with the AWS Generative AI Innovation Center, benchmarks Trainium at about 60% more input audio seconds per dollar than its GPU baselines. Hugging Face says the backend makes Trainium a native target for Transformers and Diffusers through a fully open-source stack, with TRL enabling fine-tuning and reinforcement learning.
highlights: Trainium becomes a native PyTorch backend: no model rewrites required
Stock Transformers and Diffusers definitions run through a fully open-source stack
Cartesia kept PyTorch code nearly unchanged, hand-writing kernels only for hot layers
Deepgram benchmarks ~60% more input audio seconds per dollar than GPU baselines
Hugging Face frames it as practical silicon neutrality for 6M+ open models
TRL supports fine-tuning and RL on Trainium
